content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Introduction to Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) represent a foundational class of artificial neural networks designed specifically for processing sequential data. Unlike traditional feedforward networks that assume all inputs and outputs are independent of each other, RNNs possess a hidden state that captures information about what has been calculated so far."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Architecture of an RNN"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"At the core of an RNN is a recurrently connected hidden layer. At each time step t, the hidden state h_t is updated based on the current input x_t and the previous hidden state h_{t-1}."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Input vector x_t: Represents the feature vector at time step t."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Hidden state h_t: Acts as the memory of the network, capturing sequential dynamics."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Weights W_hh, W_xh, W_hy: Shared parameters across all time steps that govern hidden-to-hidden, input-to-hidden, and hidden-to-output transformations."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Mathematical Formulation"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"The forward pass equations for a standard Elman RNN are defined as follows:"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"h_t = tanh(W_hh * h_{t-1} + W_xh * x_t + b_h)\ny_t = softmax(W_hy * h_t + b_y)"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT)"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Training an RNN requires accumulating gradients across time steps, an algorithm known as Backpropagation Through Time (BPTT). BPTT unfolds the RNN along the temporal dimension, transforming it into a deep feedforward network where weights are shared across layers."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 1: Perform the forward pass over the entire sequence and compute the loss at each time step."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 2: Compute the total loss L as the sum of losses across all time steps: L = sum(L_t)."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Step 3: Propagate the gradients backward from the final time step down to the first time step, accumulating derivatives with respect to the shared weight matrices."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Challenges in BPTT: Vanishing and Exploding Gradients"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Because BPTT involves repeated multiplication of the recurrent weight matrix W_hh, gradients can grow exponentially (exploding gradients) or shrink exponentially to zero (vanishing gradients) over long sequences. This makes standard RNNs notoriously difficult to train on long-range dependencies."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"Mitigating Gradient Issues"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"To combat these limitations, advanced architectures like Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) introduce gating mechanisms. These gates allow gradients to flow unimpeded through an additive error carousels, mitigating the vanishing gradient problem."}]
